## Reproducing the outputs

The Nix flake pins the Python and `uv` toolchain. `pyproject.toml` defines
direct dependencies and version constraints; `uv.lock` records the exact
resolved versions and distribution SHA-256 hashes. The Docker image uses the
same flake and a fixed Nix base-image digest. On Linux, run:

```sh
nix develop --command sh scripts/setup-env.sh
nix develop --command .venv/bin/python scripts/generate_all.py --check
```

Or use Docker, without installing Python packages on the host:

```sh
docker build -t printables-check .
docker run --rm --network none printables-check
```

To write regenerated files into your checkout, bind-mount it and omit
`--check`:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/workspace" printables-check \
  nix develop --offline --command /opt/printables-venv/bin/python scripts/generate_all.py
```

For the CadQuery designs, `--check` compares STL, PNG and report files
byte-for-byte with the committed artifacts, and fails if files are added or
missing. CI performs that check inside the container with
networking disabled. The OpenSCAD slipper stand is a v0.3 snapshot: the same
command validates its committed printable meshes and report, without regenerating
its geometry or previews. See its README for separate regeneration commands.

When deliberately updating a dependency, edit `pyproject.toml`, regenerate
the lock, then rebuild and run the container check:

```sh
nix develop --command uv lock
```

## GitHub Pages site

`scripts/build_site.py` builds the static site from each design's `design.toml` (title, summary, status, cover image and parts list) and its `README.md`. The design table above is generated from the same files. The notes are converted by `scripts/markdown_subset.py`, which supports only the Markdown used in this repository (headings, paragraphs, flat `-` and numbered lists, pipe tables, fenced code, code spans, `**strong**`, links and images) and fails the build on anything else. To build and check the site into `.work/site`:

```sh
nix develop --command .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests
nix develop --command .venv/bin/python scripts/build_site.py --check
```

After adding a design or changing a `design.toml`, run `scripts/build_site.py --write-readme` to update the table. The check fails when the table is out of date, when a relative link is broken, or when a vendored file differs from its recorded hash. To preview the site locally, serve `.work/site` with any static file server, for example `python -m http.server -d .work/site`.

The 3D viewer uses three.js r186. The files in `site/vendor/three/` are taken from the pinned upstream Git commit listed in `site/vendor/three.toml`, not from the npm registry. `scripts/vendor_three.py` fetches them again and requires the recorded SHA-256 hashes; `--check` verifies the committed files offline. To update three.js, change the tag and commit in the manifest, review the upstream diff, then run the script with `--record`.

CI builds the site on every pull request and deploys it to GitHub Pages on pushes to `main`. The repository's Pages source must be set to "GitHub Actions".
